purpose: Concrete analytical fixtures for the four minimum planned cases; not flight data, a physical calibration, or a released schema.

oracle.basis: By construction, a constant ideal force vector [2,0,0] newtons acts for 3 synthetic seconds. Its time integral is [6,0,0] newton-seconds.
oracle.independence: The expected answer comes from the stated force-time construction, not the exporter label, output magnitude, or generated expected file. The navigation verification lead must separately review and control the derivation before execution.
oracle.limits: This ideal analytical oracle can challenge software interpretation for this fixture. It does not establish the physical meaning or calibration of any real supplier or legacy data. A provenance-supported physical paired sample remains missing.
oracle.comparison: Exact identifiers/version/unit semantics. The integer values in this illustrative fixture have an exact analytical expected value; the implementation-specific comparison rule must be agreed before execution. No physical measurement tolerance is supplied.

samples.expected: Candidate acceptance only after complete-path output matches the independent analytical expectation and all other applicable checks.

A schema/unit parser may accept the syntax; the independent acceptance comparison must identify 7 versus the expected 6 and withhold/quarantine the test transaction. It cannot prove universal runtime detection of mislabeled physical data.
